ConnectionStrings.// DefaultConnection: SECRET — do NOT commit a value here. Cloud: set env var ConnectionStrings__DefaultConnection. Local install: the installer writes appsettings.Production.json. Dev: appsettings.Development.json.

Backup.// PgDumpPath: Path to pg_dump.exe (bundled with PostgreSQL). Set by the server installer; empty in dev/Cloud (backup then reports 'pg_dump introuvable').
Backup.// DefaultDestination: Fallback backup destination folder when the admin doesn't supply one.
Backup.// TimeoutSeconds: Max seconds a pg_dump run may take before it is killed (default 1800).

MinIO.// AccessKey: SECRET — supply via env (MinIO__AccessKey) or user-secrets. The published default minioadmin is rejected outside Development.
MinIO.// SecretKey: SECRET — supply via env (MinIO__SecretKey) or user-secrets.

Reminders.// Channels: Enabled reminder channels. Values: "Sms", "WhatsApp". Empty = reminders disabled (nothing is enqueued).
Reminders.// LeadTimesHours: Preferred lead-time tiers (hours before the appointment). The largest tier still in the future is used.
Reminders.// MinLeadHours: Below this many hours before the appointment, no reminder is scheduled.
Reminders.// MaxRetries: Max transient send attempts before a reminder is marked Failed.

Sms.// ApiUrl: HTTP SMS gateway endpoint (JSON POST). Empty = SMS disabled.
Sms.// SenderId: Alphanumeric sender ID shown to the patient.
Sms.// ApiKey: SECRET — do NOT put the value here. Set env var Reminders__Sms__ApiKey (or user-secrets/.local).

WhatsApp.// ApiUrl: WhatsApp Business Graph API base URL, e.g. https://graph.facebook.com/v21.0. Empty = WhatsApp disabled.
WhatsApp.// TemplateName: Approved utility template name (single body parameter carries the reminder text).
WhatsApp.// AccessToken: SECRET — do NOT put the value here. Set env var Reminders__WhatsApp__AccessToken (or user-secrets/.local).

Meta.// _comment: WhatsApp Embedded Signup (Cloud onboarding). Endpoints 404 in Local mode.
Meta.// AppId: Meta app id used to init the Embedded-Signup SDK and the code→token exchange. Public value.
Meta.// AppSecret: SECRET — do NOT put the value here. Set env var Meta__AppSecret (or user-secrets/.local).
Meta.// GraphApiVersion: Graph API version, e.g. v21.0. Defaults to v21.0 when empty.

GoogleCalendar.// ClientSecret: SECRET — do NOT commit a value here. Set env var GoogleCalendar__ClientSecret (or user-secrets/.local).
GoogleCalendar.// RefreshToken: SECRET — do NOT commit a value here. Normally persisted at runtime via IGoogleTokenStore (.local/); env fallback GoogleCalendar__RefreshToken.

Cors.// AllowedOrigins: Optional (FR-E1). Extra CORS origins unioned with FrontendUrl for LAN clients, e.g. ["https://clinic-server:5001"]. Empty = FrontendUrl only (Cloud default).

Clients.// Clients: The native shells' version floor (mobile-native-shells AC-28/AC-34), published anonymously at GET /api/meta/client-requirements and enforced by ClientVersionMiddleware. Operator-owned: raising the floor needs no code change and no restart.
Clients.// MinimumShellVersion: Oldest shell this server still answers. A shell below it gets 426 { error, code: client_too_old } on every /api route but the one above. EMPTY = no floor, which is the deliberate default and the safe failure mode — a typo here must refuse nothing, never everything. Browsers send no version header at all and are never affected.
Clients.// CurrentShellVersion: The release the stores currently carry. Told to a refused client so it can say what to update to; never compared against anything.
Clients.// StoreUrls: Where a refused client is sent. Each client reads the one for the machine it runs on; empty = that platform has nowhere to send anyone yet, and the client must show no link rather than a broken one.
Clients.// StoreUrls:Windows: NOT a store listing: the desktop shell is an installer you host yourself, so this is a plain download URL for the newest ClinicManagement client installer. It lives beside the two store entries because 'where does this client get a newer build' is one question with three answers.

Subscription.// Subscription: A cabinet's dated right to record new work (clinic-subscription). ⚠️ There is deliberately NO 'Enabled' key here: WHETHER subscriptions are enforced is decided by the deployment's KIND (DeploymentProfile.RequiresSubscription, true for HostedMultiTenant only — AC-7.3), so no operator setting can turn a clinic's own PC into one that refuses its own patient records. Everything in this section is a value the enforcement uses, never the switch. No secret-bearing key.
Subscription.// TrialDays: Free days a new cabinet arrives with, the creation day counting as day 1 (AC-1.1): 30 → created 10 Aug, may work all of 8 Sep. Recorded as the opening ledger entry's DURATION, so changing this later moves NO existing cabinet's end date (AC-1.5/EC-12) — each date is folded from what was recorded. Out of range or absent = 30.
Subscription.// Plans: What « Abonnement » quotes per forfait, in dinars (AC-2.1/AC-2.4 — a price must not be compiled in). A missing or non-positive figure reads as « tarif non publié », NOT as 0,000 DT: an unfilled deployment saying it publishes no price is true, a zero is not. The annual figure is not derived from the monthly one — it is a discount, so both are stated. The plan is a label and a price; it gates nothing.
Subscription.// PaymentInstructions: French text telling the cabinet how to pay — bank details and what reference to quote. Shown on « Abonnement » and never behind a disclosure: it is the one thing an expired cabinet opens that screen for.
Subscription.// Contact: Who the cabinet reaches to sort out a payment. Empty = that line is not rendered rather than rendered blank.

Push.// Push: OS push notifications for the native shells (mobile-native-shells Part 6). Per INSTALL, not per clinic: there is one mobile app, so one Firebase project and one Apple team. A platform is sendable only when the deployment profile permits it (SelfHostedLan never does) AND all three of its values below are present — GET /api/push-devices/availability reports that verdict per platform, and an unsupported platform is REFUSED at registration rather than queued.
Push.// Secrets: Never commit ServiceAccountKey or PrivateKey. Supply them as environment variables (Push__Fcm__ServiceAccountKey, Push__Apns__PrivateKey) or through the operator-owned appsettings.Production.json.

Fcm.// ApiUrl: Optional. FCM HTTP v1 send endpoint; {projectId} is substituted. Empty = the documented default.

Apns.// ApiUrl: Optional. APNs endpoint; {token} is substituted with the device token. Empty = the production default (api.push.apple.com).
Apns.// BundleId: The apns-topic APNs refuses a mismatch on — the shell's bundle identifier, which Part 8 settles and which cannot be changed after first submission.

Push.// Dispatch: Bounds on one tick of PushDispatchJob. PerClinicDispatchBound is the fairness cap that stops one practice's backlog owning every tick on a hosted install.
Push.// RetentionDays: How long a Sent/Failed row is kept. Blocked and Pending rows are NEVER purged — a blocked row is the evidence of what is misconfigured.

Https.// CertPath: Optional. Path to a PFX server certificate. Local mode: leave EMPTY to have the server self-generate a CA + cert into .local/ (FR-E2); if set, the file must exist or the server refuses to start (no silent HTTP downgrade). Cloud: empty = plain HTTP (host/proxy terminates TLS).
Https.// CertPassword: Never commit a value here (S3/Finding 5). The PFX password is sourced from the gitignored .local/ store (self-generated certs) or an environment variable / user-secret (operator-supplied certs).

Hosting.// Urls: Optional (FR-E4). Bind address(es) when no HTTPS cert is set, e.g. "http://0.0.0.0:5000". Empty = ASPNETCORE_URLS / host default.
Hosting.// Ports: HTTP/HTTPS ports Kestrel binds in Local mode (Cloud: only when Https:CertPath is set).
Hosting.// WebPort: Local mode (S4): the localhost HTTP port the co-located Next server listens on; the Kestrel front door reverse-proxies non-/api routes here. Inert in Cloud.
Hosting.// TrustPort: Local mode (P8): cleartext LAN port serving ONLY /api/trust — the page a phone uses to install the CA before it can trust HTTPS. Every other path on this port is refused (TrustPortGate). Must differ from HttpPort/HttpsPort/WebPort; 0 disables the trust page. Inert in Cloud.
